newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices gain on storage demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices gain on storage demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices resumed their upward march Thursday, still driven by decent storage demand despite relatively mild U.S. weather and forecasts for more of the same next week, traders said.
And with cash-to-futures spreads still widening, most expected the stepped up pace of injections to continue to prop physical prices near-term.
"We're going into storage big time right now...you have to, the spreads work," said one cash trader.
U.S. Gulf Coast swing prices jumped five to 10 cents today to near the $1.90 level, more than 10 cents over Sept indices.
In the Midcontinent, prices firmed nearly five cents to the mid-$1.70s, about 10 cents over September indices. Gas in Chicago was a couple of cents higher in the mid-$1.90s or better.
West Texas gas on El Paso Permian was several cents higher in the mid-to-high $1.60s, almost five cents over index. South Texas gained a nickel to $1.80-1.85, about five cents over Sept 1 levels.
In New York, swing city gate prices rose more than five cents to the $2.10-2.15 area.
